explanation: The accepted AXI-Lite write address is deliberately altered with XOR 4 before being stored. Consequently, every register-side write presents an address whose bit 2 is inverted, while the checker compares it against the original handshaken address. This directly causes the `register_payload` failures; write and response progress still completes because the control handshake logic is otherwise functioning.
evidence: tb.sv line 36 queues the unmodified `s_axil_awaddr` on each AW handshake.
tb.sv line 40 requires `reg_wr_addr === address_queue[sent]` and reports `register_payload` on a mismatch.
axil_reg_if_wr.v line 93 drives `reg_wr_addr` from the altered `s_axil_awaddr_reg`.
sim.log reports 12 `register_payload` errors while all 12 writes and responses complete, consistent with systematic payload corruption rather than a progress failure.
